articles.body: BHOPAL: A Tikamgarh man’s complaint against a television that allegedly stopped displaying pictures has been rejected by Madhya Pradesh State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. The commission held that he failed to establish that the set had developed a manufacturing defect during the warranty period or that he had formally complained to the seller.The commission dismissed the appeal on Nov 20, upholding Tikamgarh District Consumer Commission’s order rejecting his complaint. Manoj Kumar Dixit had purchased a television for Rs 31,500 from an electronics retailer on Nov 10, 2015. He claimed that the set came with a three-year warranty but developed a problem with its picture display during the warranty period. He sought repair or replacement of the television.Dixit said he subsequently sent a notice to the seller and also raised a complaint through the company’s toll-free number on Oct 25, 2018. However, he alleged that no action was taken. The retailer denied responsibility, arguing that it was only the retailer and not the manufacturer. It said Dixit had never complained to it about the television being defective. The manufacturer and its other respondent entity did not appear before the district commission, which proceeded ex parte against them.Challenging the dismissal of his complaint, Dixit argued before the state commission that the district commission had failed to properly examine the documents and submissions on record.However, the state commission found that he had not specified the date on which the television developed the alleged fault. He had also failed to produce an expert report establishing a manufacturing defect or documents showing that he had complained to the respondents about the problem. The commission observed that, in the absence of such evidence, it could not be established that the television had developed a manufacturing defect during the warranty period. articles.title: Gwalior man applies hair-removal cream bought on Flipkart, suffers severe burns and lands in ICU; consumer commission orders Rs 88,065 compensation
articles.summary: BHOPAL: A Gwalior man who suffered severe burns after applying a hair-removal cream bought online had to be admitted to the ICU of a private hospital.
articles.body: BHOPAL: A Gwalior man who suffered severe burns after applying a hair-removal cream bought online had to be admitted to the ICU of a private hospital. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held the online seller and manufacturer liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practices, directing them to pay him Rs 88,065.The commission passed the order on November 12 in a complaint filed by Punit Chugvani against Flipkart and the manufacturer of the product, Cura Men Hair Remover Cream.Chugvani bought the cream on July 5, 2025. He said he first tested it on a small patch of skin on July 11, following the prescribed instructions. When no adverse reaction appeared, he applied it to his chest. He soon experienced a burning sensation and immediately washed off the cream.However, his skin was badly burnt. He consulted a local doctor on July 12 as the condition worsened. When he did not get relief, he went to Apollo Hospital in Gwalior the next day. Doctors admitted him to the ICU, and he remained hospitalised until July 17.Chugvani claimed that he spent Rs 1.5 lakh on treatment. He alleged that he informed the seller and manufacturer and was initially assured that his medical expenses would be reimbursed, but they later refused to pay. He subsequently sent them a legal notice on December 23, 2025.The commission noted that Flipkart did not appear during the proceedings despite receiving notice. The manufacturer appeared through a lawyer but did not file a proper reply to the complaint. The commission said the manufacturer's photographic copies of documents could not be considered as admissible evidence.The commission relied on Chugvani's affidavit and medical records, including the Apollo Hospital discharge summary, which specifically recorded burning and redness on the chest wall and neck following the use of the hair-removal cream.It also noted that neither respondent had challenged his account or produced any investigation report to establish that the product was free from manufacturing defects or safe for use on the human body. The commission concluded that the cream had caused the physical problems and that selling such a defective product amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.However, while Chugvani claimed treatment expenses of Rs 1.5 lakh, the commission found that the final hospital bill on record was for Rs 81,065. It directed Flipkart and the manufacturer, jointly or separately, to reimburse this amount within 45 days.They were also ordered to pay Rs 5,000 for mental and physical suffering and Rs 2,000 towards litigation expenses. articles.body: NEW DELHI: DMK student wing members hung an effigy of TVK MLA C Arul Vignesh from a bridge in Vandavasi, Tiruvannamalai district, on Thursday, demanding his arrest over a sexual harassment complaint filed by a woman district collector.The protesters staged the demonstration by recreating a scene from actor-politician Vijay’s film Theri, in which a culprit is shown hanging from a bridge. They raised slogans calling for the arrest of the Kallakurichi MLA, who has been accused of sending inappropriate messages to the district collector.(Movie scene refrenced by DMK student wing)Police later removed the effigy from the bridge.A case was registered against Vignesh on November 24 after the collector submitted a complaint to Kallakurichi superintendent of police I Shanaz. The complaint alleged that the MLA made inappropriate, sexually coloured remarks to the officer. Vignesh has denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated.The case was registered under Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including those relating to sexual harassment, stalking and assault or criminal force against a public servant.The complaint followed months of alleged inaction. Sources said the collector had informed senior officials, including chief secretary M Sai Kumar, about the MLA’s conduct on July 31. She later submitted a written complaint to the police on November 23.The National Commission for Women took suo motu cognisance of the matter on November 15 and urged the Tamil Nadu DGP to ensure an impartial inquiry. The Madras high court had earlier observed that it could not act solely on media reports without a complaint from the person concerned.On Wednesday, DMK leader and leader of the opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin submitted a representation to DGP Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, seeking Vignesh’s arrest and transfer of the investigation to the CBI.Udhayanidhi alleged that the state government had failed to act on the officer’s earlier communication and questioned chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s silence on the issue. articles.title: How replacing Delhi's non-BS-VI vehicles may cost owners close to Rs 76,000 crore
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Over 4 out of every 10 petrol cars registered in Delhi over the past 15 years fall in the below BS 6 category, while four out of every 10
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Over 4 out of every 10 petrol cars registered in Delhi over the past 15 years fall in the below BS 6 category, while four out of every 10 petrol two-wheelers are likely to be affected if the Supreme Court's observation on restricting such vehicles were to be implemented.This point to a potentially significant impact on private vehicle owners, particularly those using older petrol vehicles.A review of vehicle registration data from 2012 to 2026 shows that nearly 8.4 lakh out of 18.9 lakh petrol cars registered in Delhi during this period were below BS 6, accounting for 44.3% of the total. Similarly, 17.3 lakh out of 42.8 lakh petrol two-wheelers registered during these 15 years fell in the below BS 6 category, accounting for 40.3%.However, these figures do not represent the number of such vehicles currently running on Delhi’s roads. Some vehicles registered in the city over the years may have become non-operational, while others may have been sold outside the city.Under the existing guidelines, petrol vehicles are allowed a lifespan of 15 years in Delhi-NCR. As a result, many owners may continue using their vehicles until they approach the end of this permitted period, while others may sell them to buyers in different cities rather than scrap them, said a senior official.At the same time, the number of below BS-VI vehicles entering Delhi cannot be assessed through the capital’s registration figures alone. Vehicles registered in other parts of the country, particularly neighbouring NCR cities, also enter and run on Delhi’s roads every day.The broader registration data for all vehicle categories in Delhi over the past 10 calendar years, from 2017 to 2026, presents a different picture. Of the 54.1 lakh vehicles registered during this period, 15.1 lakh, or 27.9%, were below BS-VI standards. This means ne­a­rly three out of every 10 vehicl­es registered during these ye­a­rs fall in the category that cou­ld be affected by such a curb.The transition to BS-VI is particularly evident in the year-wise figures. In 2019, 94.5% of all vehicles registe­red in Delhi were below BS-VI, with only 25,750 of the 4.7 lakh vehicles falling in the BS-VI category. In 2020, however, the share of below BS -VI vehicles dropped sharply to 21.24%.From 2021 onwards, the share of below BS-VI vehicles among annual registrations remained negligible, ranging between 0.02% and 0.10%.BS-VI, or Bharat Stage-VI, is the sixth stage of India’s vehicle emission standards and imposes stricter limits on pollutants released by vehicles compared with earlier standards, including BS-IV. The norms regulate emissions such as nitrogen oxides, particulate matter, hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide. The objective is to reduce the amount of harmful pollutants released into the air by vehicles.The BS-VI standards became mandatory for new vehicle registrations from April 1, 2020 in several categories of vehicles. Vehicles manufactured under the newer standards are designed to emit lower levels of harmful pollutants, making them cleaner than vehicles complying with earlier emission norms.Supreme Court on Nov 23 orally mooted allowing only BS-VI-compliant vehicles to ply in Delhi as part of efforts to tackle air pollution particularly in winters. However, no immediate formal order enforcing such a restriction had been issued.If we assume that all petrol cars and two-wheelers that aren’t BS-VI registered in Delhi between 2012 and 2026 were to be replaced, the estimated expenditure for vehicle owners could touch Rs 75,831 crore.The calculation assumes a replacement cost of Rs 8 lakh per car and Rs 50,000 per motorcycle. Between 2012 and 2026, Delhi recorded 8.4 lakh such petrol cars. The replacement cost would translate into nearly Rs 67,182 crore, that for replacing 17.3 lakh two-wheelers would be nearly Rs 8,648 crore. The total cost would be nearly Rs 75,831 crore.A senior official, however, said estimating the replacement cost assumes that owner of a below BS-VI vehicle would buy a new vehicle if restrictions are imposed, which may not necessarily be the case.Many may choose not to replace their vehicles at all, particularly when factors like age and migration are considered. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: US-based gangster Himanshu Bhau's gang is suspected to be behind the killing of four men who were shot dead in a suspected gang war at Milan
articles.body: NEW DELHI: US-based gangster Himanshu Bhau's gang is suspected to be behind the killing of four men who were shot dead in a suspected gang war at Milan Dhaba on Delhi Road near Kharawar village in Haryana's Rohtak district early on Thursday.Bhau was recently apprehended in Las Vegas along with another gangster Neeraj Faridpuria.The incident happened around 1am when the victims were eating at the establishment. At least five armed assailants arrived in a car and opened indiscriminate fire.The sudden gunfire triggered panic at the venue, forcing bystanders and staff to scramble for cover as the shooters fled the scene.The deceased have been identified as Rinku (son of Jagbir), Vineet (son of Jaybir), and Ganju—all residents of Dighal village in Jhajjar district—along with Himanshu (son of Rajbir), a resident of the Beri area.Initial investigations indicate that all four victims were shooters affiliated with the Sunny Ritoliya gang (also linked to the Baba gang). Police suspect the attack was carried out by rival operatives belonging to the Himanshu Bhau gang.Investigators noted that gang leaders Sunny Ritoliya and Himanshu Bhau both hail from Ritoli village and share a long-standing, violent rivalry that has previously led to multiple clashes.Following the incident, personnel from the IMT police station, along with senior officials including Inspector General (IG) Hamid Akhtar and Superintendent of Police (SP) Gaurav Rajpurohit, reached the spot.Police are currently reviewing footage from nearby CCTV cameras and have deployed multiple teams to trace and apprehend the absconding assailants.The murders are being seen as the fallout of the rivalry with Baba gang. articles.title: 'Sathyameva' OTT release date announced: Rony David Raj leads crime drama; missing girl mystery forms central plot; where to watch
articles.summary: Rony David Raj is set to headline the upcoming Malayalam crime drama 'Sathyameva'.
articles.body: Rony David Raj is set to headline the upcoming Malayalam crime drama 'Sathyameva'. The series is set against a courtroom backdrop and the story revolves around a disgraced lawyer, a man searching for his missing daughter and a case that could uncover secrets buried for two decades.'Sathyameva' follows a lawyer seeking redemptionThe series centers on Rajaram, whose legal career takes a setback after he fails to save an innocent client. The incident continues to haunt him, leaving him away from the courtroom. However, an unexpected request gives him an opportunity to take up a case again.A man whom people consider to be mentally unstable approaches Rajaram with what he describes as his final request. He wants the lawyer to find his daughter, who disappeared twenty years ago. Rajaram decides to take up the matter and begins investigating the circumstances surrounding her disappearance.A missing girl case brings buried secrets to lightAs Rajaram follows the clues, the investigation gradually leads him towards secrets that have remained hidden for years. The case becomes more complicated as he attempts to establish what happened to the missing girl.For the lawyer, the investigation is about more than reuniting a father with his daughter. It also offers him an opportunity to confront his past failure and seek redemption. His pursuit of the truth places justice at the center of the story, while the courtroom setting adds another layer to the crime drama.Rony David Raj leads the cast of 'Sathyameva'Rony David Raj plays the lead role of Rajaram. The supporting cast includes Deepu Karunakaran, Meenakshi Unnikrishnan and Jayaraj Kozhikode. 'Sathyameva' will premiere on November 27, 2026, on ZEE5's Malayalam platform. Sharing the announcement, the makers wrote, "When the fight for justice begins, every testimony matters. But will the truth survive the fire of allegations? Sathyameva – Premieres 27th November, only on Malayalam Zee 5."The team had previously shared another poster to build interest in the series. Its caption read, "Behind every face lies a story. But when the truth comes out, who will have the courage to face it?."On the other hand, Rony David's most recent films include 'Dose' (2026) and Prithviraj Sukumaran's 'I, Nobody' (2026).
